Standard operator precedence rules would parse it as `p_3(Kyler) ∧ (¬p_5(Kyler) → p_4(Kyler))`, meaning 'Kyler creates strapless gowns AND (if Kyler does not use luxury fabrics then Kyler inspires confidence in his clients)'. However, the natural language statement 'If Kyler creates strapless gowns and does not use luxury fabrics, then he inspires confidence in his clients' implies the entire conjunction `(p_3(Kyler) ∧ ¬p_5(Kyler))` as the antecedent of the implication. Therefore, the correct FOL should be `(p_3(Kyler) ∧ ¬p_5(Kyler)) → p_4(Kyler)`.
